title: trace identity hop sleuthing notebook
body:
High-level summary:

Short: trying to isolate where traces are being severed / identity-mapped in the ingest pipeline. Symptoms: customer traces show gaps (missing service hops), trace_id preserved in headers but spans not coming through downstream services. Metric drop in 'ingest.traces.received' for a 30m window during the incident.

Why I care: this is producing false negatives in SLO alerting (missing errors) and appears correlated with sample-rate changes we didn't expect. Need reproducible steps and quick mitigations (restart collector vs gateway change).

Observed timeline (local testing & infra logs):
- 2024-09-18 09:42 UTC: first alert, grafana panel 'ingest.traces.received' dropped from ~12k/m to ~2k/m for sampler service-type 'edge-gateway'
- 2024-09-18 09:47 UTC: noticed traces arriving at edge with header X-Trace-Id still present but downstream services show new trace_ids or missing parent span
- 2024-09-18 10:05 UTC: toggled gateway sampler fraction from 0.1 -> 0.2 as a test; no immediate change
- 2024-09-18 10:23 UTC: restarted otel-collector in region-us-west-2 (temporary mitigation), small bump in charts for ~7m then dropped again

Commands I ran (notes and outputs pasted as-is):
- curl to verify header passthrough from client -> gateway:
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "X-Obs-Trace: 0000000000000001" https://gateway.internal/test-endpoint
  -> Response headers: X-Obs-Trace: 0000000000000001, server: envoy
  // So gateway preserves header on 200 responses for simple GET

- kafka consumer check (consumer-group = obs-ingest-backend):
  kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group obs-ingest-backend --describe
  -> LAG: shows small lag on topic tx-traces-raw, consumer 'obs-ingest-01' had occasional rebalances at 09:40

- quick grep of raw payloads in s3 (one sample):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-obs-raw/2024-09-18/09/trace_batch_09_41.json - | jq '.spans | length'
  -> 6 (but parent_id missing on span[2])

- otelcol config dump on collector pod (use kubectl exec):
  kubectl -n telemetry exec -it otel-collector-0 -- cat /conf/otel-collector-config.yaml | sed -n '1,240p'
  -> sampler: parentbased_traceidratio 0.1, receivers: jaeger/grpc/http, exporters: kafka, redis-cache (prefix obs-prefix)

- redis tl;dr check on kv cache: TTL distribution seemed weird:
  redis-cli -h redis.ingest.local --scan --pattern 'obs-prefix:*' | wc -l -> ~120k keys
  sample TTL: redis-cli ttl obs-prefix:trace:0000000000000001 -> -1 (no ttl)
  hypothesis: cached KV entries for trace routing not expiring, causing sticky routing to an old/retired collector pool

What I observed in traces (examples):
- Case A: incoming request with trace_id 0xabc arrives at gateway with client span. Gateway forwards to svc-a. svc-a reports spans with trace_id 0xabc but parent_id=0xdeadbeef (mismatch). svc-b downstream never shows svc-a spans (so tooling links them as separate traces).
- Case B: incoming with trace_id 0x123 header is stripped by collector on re-ingest, new trace_id 0x7f4 created; root span shows 'ingest.processor: new-root'

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sampling policy mismatch between gateway and collector: parent-based sampler on collector may be ignoring externally supplied sampled flag and resampling, creating new root spans or dropping children. (probable)
2) KV-routing cache (redis) holds a mapping for trace -> collector_id that points to removed pool, causing re-emit to older collector running different otel config (old sampler). (medium)
3) Envoy sidecar or ingress rewriting trace headers for certain content-types (multipart, gRPC vs http) due to envoy filter. (low-medium)
4) Kafka consumer rebalances + batch-windowing causes partial batches where parent span not in same batch and dropped because of dedupe logic downstream. (medium)
5) Edge gateway rewriting TraceParent -> custom header and a buggy codec loses traceparent when body > 32k (rare). (low)

Notes-to-self / quick repro ideas:
- Reproduce locally by running gateway + small collector with different sampler configs and send a few synthetic requests where I intentionally set traceparent header. See if collector produces new root.
- Use k6 load test with header injection and small body sizes to check if body length correlates with header loss (script attached in linked_artifacts).
- For KV-cache theory: run redis monitor while issuing synthetic requests to see writes and TTL operations. Check whether writes set TTL or persist.

Commands to repro locally (sketch):
- start collector with sampler=0 in docker-compose and another with sampler=1; run a tiny python http client that sets Traceparent and sends 10 requests; observe spans in jaeger query UI (local).
- run: python3 -c 'import requests
for i in range(10):
  h = {"traceparent":"00-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-01"}
  r = requests.post("http://localhost:8080/push", headers=h, data="x")
  print(r.status_code)'

Failed attempts and weirdness:
- I tried flipping collector sampling to always_on for a minute — got more spans but still some hops missing. That suggests header loss earlier in pipeline rather than collector drop alone.
- Restarting a single collector temporarily increases received metric then falls back -> possible race/heartbeat issue on route table refresh in routing service.
- Observed one gateway log line: 'trace-router: mapped trace_id 0x123 -> collector_id null, defaulting to bucket-7' immediately followed by 'kafka-producer: send failed: partition_not_leader' at 09:42:07. Producer error could trigger retries and reorder which might explain missing parent/child alignment in small windows.

Next debugging steps (short list):
- [ ] Add extra logging in gateway: log x-obs-trace header and route mapping decision (short-term debug build to a canary)
- [ ] Temporarily enable debug sampling passthrough in collector (honor incoming sampled flag) on one canary collector and observe
- [ ] Instrument redis writes with EXPIRE to ensure TTLs; if current writes don't set TTL, rollback to previous library version that did (if applicable)
- [ ] Run kafka-producer client with idempotent writes temporarily disabled/enabled to see reorder behavior impact
- [ ] Create a Grafana temporary panel that correlates kafka producer errors + consumer rebalances + ingest.traces.received (minute resolution)

Notes for follow-up with ops / infra:
- Ask infra to check network flaps between kafka brokers 09:35-09:50 (quick check: broker-2 had an OOM event at 09:38 according to node exporter alert)
- Confirm if any autoscaling event removed collectors at 09:40 (scale down triggered by a mistaken mem metric)

Questions unresolved / things to watch:
- If the kv-cache is sticky, how was it seeded? Is there a side-effect in the route-writing code that persists keys without TTL on error paths?
- Is there a known bug in otelcol exporter v0.62 that transforms traceparent into new root on exporter failure? PR referenced in linked_artifacts maybe related.

Quick mitigation options (ranked):
- 1) Force collectors to honor incoming sampling flag (low risk, quick deploy to one region)
- 2) Add short TTL refresh process for kv-cache entries and prune stale keys (medium risk)
- 3) Add a gateway fallback that forwards trace as 'x-obs-trace-raw' (keep original header) until root cause diagnosed (medium-high)

Personal notes: keep this doc as the running scratchpad. If I make any small scripts I will paste them here. If I open a formal postmortem or runbook update, move finalized bits to Confluence and link from this doc.

Recent small experiments (results):
- Set sampler at gateway to always_on and collector to always_on for 10m -> total ingested spans 2.8x but missing-hop ratio stayed ~4%
- Disabled kafka idempotence -> slight drop in partition_not_leader logs but no improvement in missing-hop ratio

Immediate ask to team: if anyone has seen header rewriting in envoy filters (esp older versions) please ping me. Also ask release-eng if any telemetry PRs touched kafka producer config around 2024-09-15.

End of notes for now.

-- maya
